title: Emergency Action Plan, chemical distributor, Oregon

must.line: kind: program (accept "policy" as a near miss, note it)
1. No procedure for reporting a fire or emergency. Citation contains "1910.38(c)(1)" OR the Oregon rule "OAR 437-002-0042" (state plan).
must.corrected: 2026-09-27: was citation "1910.38(c)(1)" only. Now accepts the GOVERNING STATE rule or the federal one. Oregon runs its own OSHA state plan, so OAR 437-002-0042 is what binds a Portland employer and 29 CFR 1910.38 is the standard Oregon adopted; every Opus configuration found this gap in every run and claude-opus-5-5 failed all three lines for citing only the OAR. *** THE OAR PARAGRAPH LETTER IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED. *** The models asserted a mapping (reporting=(2)(c), critical operations=(2)(d), contact=(2)(f)) and NOBODY HAS CHECKED IT against the OAR text. Encoding a paragraph on the strength of model output would put an unverified regulatory claim into an answer key, where this suite could never question it again. So the rule number is required and the paragraph is not, on the OAR side only.
